name: W. Leland, livery stable

proprietors.name: Warren Leland
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Warren Leland is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at livery_stable_keeper in the south division (slot trade_households:persons/male/20_29/south/family/trade:livery_stable_keeper:046), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a livery stable kept by a south-division household deals this house onto Dearborn Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a livery stable keeper the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Warren Leland (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real livery stable in the south division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a livery stable, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Warren Leland at livery stable keeper because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and the occupation names the house: a livery stable keeper keeps a livery stable, and the register prints two of them — Lathrop Johnson & Co., livery, and the Livery Stable at the Point — against a census that enumerates neither. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 2 head(s) at livery stable keeper in the south division and the occupation names the house: a livery stable keeper keeps a livery stable, and the register prints two of them — Lathrop Johnson & Co., livery, and the Livery Stable at the Point — against a census that enumerates neither. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the form 'Lathrop Johnson & Co., livery' prints, with the firm cut to the sole keeper it is — an initial and a surname, as 'S. Foot' and 'A. Garrett' print elsewhere in the register. The goods line is the register's own words for the trade in 'the Livery Stable at the Point'.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
